title: Cheese and Potato Pie
subtitle: A hearty Northern shortcrust pie of sharp cheddar and soft potato
excerpt: Floury potatoes and plenty of mature cheddar in a shortcrust case, baked until the lid is deep gold. A filling weeknight supper that slices cleanly hot or cold.
sourceNotes: Northern English baking tradition, drawn from mill-town pie-shop practice and adapted for a standard 23cm pie dish.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the baked pie whole or in slices. Reheat from frozen at 180C until piping hot through.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble the pie up to a day ahead and keep it chilled. Add an extra five minutes to the bake time.

content.text: This pie is built on two simple fillings: floury potatoes and sharp mature cheddar. Cook the potato through before it goes in, so the filling is soft and creamy. Let everything cool before the pastry goes on, or the base will go soggy.

items.prepNote: two thirds for the base, one third for the lid

content.text: Boil the potato cubes in well-salted water for 12 minutes until tender. Drain well and leave to steam dry for five minutes.
Mash the potato with the butter and milk until smooth. Stir in the cheddar and spring onion. Season with salt and pepper. Leave to cool completely.
Heat the oven to 200C. Roll out two thirds of the pastry and line the pie dish, leaving a short overhang at the rim.
Spoon the cooled filling into the case and spread it level.
Roll the remaining pastry for a lid. Brush the rim with beaten egg and lay the lid over the top. Press the edges firmly to seal.
Trim away the excess pastry and cut a small slit in the centre. Brush the top all over with beaten egg.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until the crust is deep golden brown. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

items.symptom: The base is soft and undercooked.
items.cause: The filling was warm when it went in, or the pie dish sat on a cold shelf.
items.fix: Always cool the filling fully. Bake on a preheated heavy baking tray for a crisper base.

items.symptom: The lid splits open during baking.
items.cause: Steam built up with nowhere to escape.
items.fix: Cut two slits in the lid before baking. One small slit is often not enough.

items.symptom: The filling is dry and crumbly.
items.cause: Too little milk or butter in the mash.
items.fix: Add an extra tablespoon of butter and a splash more milk. The mix should be soft but hold its shape.
